## Open blockers

### Scientific

| Family | Dim | Issue | Blocker |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `lpt_encoder` | I | RES-694 | No registry claim on LPT or encoder validity, cable-angle error or measurement error. |
| `lpt_encoder` | O | RES-694 | Limitations need sourced claims (attachment point vs centre of mass, single vs dual cable). |
| `load_cell_isometric` | I | RES-694 | No source on load-cell calibration error, creep or rig compliance. |
| `load_cell_isometric` | O | RES-694 | No source comparing IMTP on a load-cell rig with IMTP on a force plate. |
| `nordic_hip` | H | RES-694 | Isometric hamstring (30/90 deg) has a declared registry gap; its metric definitions cannot be sourced yet. |
| `timing_contact` | I | RES-694 | No source quantifying contact-mat switching latency or gate beam-type and trigger-height error. |
| `radar_laser` | I | RES-694 | No device-level radar or laser validity, sampling or body-point source. |
| `gnss_lps` | I | RES-694 | No registry claim on GNSS or LPS validity, sampling rate or speed and acceleration error. |
| `gnss_lps` | L | RES-703 | No audited raw GNSS or LPS dataset exists for empirical agreement (RES-666 covered summaries only). |
| `gnss_lps` | O | RES-694 | Limitations need sourced claims (Doppler vs positional speed, interpolated rates). |
| `imu` | I | RES-694 | No registry claim on IMU flight-time validity, placement or accumulated-load metrics. |
| `imu` | L | RES-703 | No audited raw IMU dataset exists for empirical agreement. |
| `imu` | O | RES-694 | Limitations need sourced claims (vendor-specific load indices, mounting site). |

## Declared non-equivalences

| Id | A | B | Statement | Study | Verdict |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| NE-001 | `gnss_lps:speed.gnss` | `radar_laser:velocity.radar` | GNSS-derived speed is not equivalent to a radar velocity trace: rates, smoothing, latency and the body point all differ. | RES-703 | open |
| NE-002 | `lpt_encoder:displacement.cable` | `force_platform:displacement.com_vertical` | LPT cable displacement is not vertical centre-of-mass or barbell displacement unless the cable geometry is declared and the attachment point's motion relative to the body is accounted for. | RES-703 | open |
| NE-003 | `lpt_encoder:power.lpt` | `force_platform:power.force_plate` | LPT power (mass x acceleration x velocity at the attachment point) and force-plate power (GRF x COM velocity) are different estimands. | RES-703 | open |
| NE-004 | `timing_contact:flight_time.contact_mat` | `force_platform:flight_time.force_plate` | Contact-mat flight time includes switching latency and threshold differences, so it is not force-plate flight time without an agreement study. | RES-703 | open |
| NE-005 | `imu:flight_time.imu` | `force_platform:flight_time.force_plate` | IMU flight time depends on mounting site and event thresholds, so it is not force-plate flight time without an agreement study. | RES-703 | open |
| NE-006 | `load_cell_isometric:peak_force.imtp_rig` | `force_platform:peak_force.imtp_plate` | IMTP peak force on a load-cell rig and on a force plate differ in rig compliance, body-weight handling and onset detection. | RES-703 | open |
| NE-007 | `timing_contact:split_time.gates` | `radar_laser:split_time.derived` | Gate splits are triggered by the first body part to break the beam; radar- or laser-derived splits track a body point. They are not interchangeable. | RES-703 | open |
| NE-008 | `radar_laser:velocity.radar_doppler` | `radar_laser:velocity.laser_differentiated` | Radar Doppler velocity and velocity differentiated from laser distance have different noise models and processing. | RES-703 | open |
| NE-009 | `gnss_lps:speed.doppler` | `gnss_lps:speed.positional` | Device Doppler speed and speed differentiated from positions are separate estimands, and both depend on vendor filtering. | RES-703 | open |
| NE-010 | `nordic_hip:force.vendor_corrected` | `nordic_hip:force.raw_cell` | Vendor-corrected Nordic or squeeze force is not raw cell force; commercial force and torque definitions are not interchangeable between vendors. | RES-703 | open |

## Quality-parity principles

| Id | Principle | Enforced by |
| -- | -- | -- |
| QP-01 | Every in-scope device family is held to the same qualification dimensions A-O. Parity is in qualification quality, not in identical algorithms. | Every family must list all fifteen dimensions (schema). |
| QP-02 | Family qualification states are computed from dimension evidence, never declared. A hand-set label that disagrees with the computed state fails. | compute_state(); declared_state check in validate(). |
| QP-03 | Importing a CSV correctly or reproducing vendor-reported numbers never qualifies any dimension. | adapter_import and vendor_reproduction evidence are non-counting. |
| QP-04 | No reference may validate itself. A reference produced by the same implementation as the engine it verifies is rejected; vendor output is never a reference (DB-07). | Reference.implementation != Reference.verifies; vendor_output rejected. RES-669 adds an import-boundary test between generators and engines. |
| QP-05 | Processing methods must suit the family's paradigm. Continuous-signal filtering is not applied to discrete timing or contact events. | processing_method.paradigms check. |
| QP-06 | Measurements from different devices are different estimands until an agreement study rules otherwise. Examples: GNSS-derived speed is not a radar velocity trace; LPT cable displacement is not vertical displacement without geometry; commercial force, torque, velocity, power and RFD definitions are not interchangeable between vendors. | non_equivalence entries need a study; an interchangeable or convertible verdict needs evidence and a basis. |
| QP-07 | Three engines are kept separate: the device processing engine (how an instrument produces observations), the assessment science engine (how a protocol produces scientific quantities) and the AI benchmark engine (how an AI system is evaluated on that work). | Families own dimensions A-F and I-M; assessment engines own G-H; M4/M5 own N. |
| QP-08 | M3 is complete only when every in-scope family computes ENGINEERING_VERIFIED. Families that cannot are reported as blocked, never silently removed from scope. SCIENTIFICALLY_QUALIFIED needs independent review (M8) and qualified grading (N). | dbs qualification gate. |
| QP-09 | Project constraints: at least two atomic commits per issue, independent verification, explicit scientific assumptions, qualified data provenance, no paid model evaluations, and no modifications to DynamisSimBench. | Review policy (not machine-checked). |
